intro: Purpose has two forms and one rule for choosing. If the person who acts is the person who benefits — same subject — use um … zu with the infinitive: Ich lerne Deutsch, um hier zu arbeiten. If the beneficiary is someone else — different subjects — use damit with a full clause, verb at the end: Ich lerne Deutsch, damit meine Kinder stolz sind. Both answer Wozu? (what for?). damit can also be used with the same subject (Ich lerne, damit ich arbeiten kann) and is never wrong, but um … zu with different subjects is impossible. The same split applies to ohne … zu / ohne dass and (an)statt … zu / (an)statt dass. Modal verbs in an um … zu clause are usually dropped (um zu arbeiten, not um arbeiten zu können — though the second exists); in a damit clause they stay (damit ich arbeiten kann). The cues in the quiz only give the content of the purpose; counting the subjects is up to you, and every natural form (um … zu, or damit with or without a modal) is accepted where it fits.
tips[0].title: Count the subjects
tips[0].text: Same subject → um … zu. Different subjects → damit. Sie spart, um ein Auto zu kaufen (she saves, she buys). Sie spart, damit ihr Sohn studieren kann (she saves, he studies).
tips[0].trap: English 'so that I can' and 'in order to' both feel like one thing. In German the subject test decides, every time.
tips[0].check.why: I cook, my friends eat: two different subjects, so damit.
tips[0].visual.root.q: Is the person doing the second action the same as the subject?
tips[1].title: damit: full clause, verb last; modals stay
tips[1].text: …, damit meine Kinder stolz sind. …, damit ihr Sohn studieren kann. …, damit du es nicht vergisst. damit is a subordinating conjunction like weil.
tips[1].check.why: damit starts a full clause: the modal stays and the conjugated verb goes to the very end.
tips[2].title: um … zu: infinitive last; modals usually dropped
tips[2].text: …, um hier zu arbeiten (not: um hier arbeiten zu können — possible but heavy). …, um pünktlich zu sein. Passive: …, um besser verstanden zu werden.
tips[2].check.why: um … zu ends with zu directly before the infinitive: um pünktlich zu sein.
tips[3].title: damit = 'so that' (someone else); um zu = 'in order to' (me)
tips[3].text: If your English sentence naturally says 'so that he/she/they …', it's damit. If it says 'to …' with no new person, it's um … zu.
tips[3].check.why: The English says 'so that her children …': a new person acts, so damit.
remember[0]: Same subject → um … zu; different subjects → damit.
remember[1]: damit clause: verb last, modal kept. um … zu: infinitive last, modal dropped.
mistakes[1].why: damit takes a full clause; um takes zu.
mistakes[2].why: zu goes directly before the infinitive at the end.
hook: Ask who does the second action, and you will know whether to say um … zu or damit every time you explain what something is for.
